candidates.rationale: Remdesivir is included as a positive-control antiviral candidate because it targets viral RNA replication biology relevant to SARS-CoV-2. It helps demonstrate that the prototype can show drugs with clear target-disease linkage when the evidence is already established. Safety and clinical-context caveats should be kept visible.
candidates.reaction_brief: Remdesivir is a nucleotide analog prodrug whose active metabolite can be incorporated during viral RNA synthesis. That interaction disrupts polymerase-driven replication and reduces viral genome production. This prototype brief summarizes known antiviral mechanism rather than a new docking result.
candidates.safety_detail: Liver enzyme elevations and infusion-related reactions are monitored risks.
candidates.data_confidence: Prototype cached result; PM/science validation required.

candidates.rationale: Dexamethasone is relevant to severe COVID-19 because it can suppress harmful inflammation rather than directly targeting the virus. It is a good demo example of repurposing through host-response biology. It should be framed carefully because timing and patient severity strongly affect usefulness.
candidates.reaction_brief: Dexamethasone binds the glucocorticoid receptor through steroid-receptor interactions and changes transcription of inflammatory mediators. The downstream effect is reduced immune overactivation in severe disease contexts. This is a host-pathway mechanism, not direct antiviral binding.
candidates.safety_detail: Can cause hyperglycemia, immunosuppression, mood changes, and infection risk.
